column1: # Light sources and their fuel. APPEND ONLY — one row per event.
# Turns of fuel left are COMPUTED from this file by `python tools/light.py`.
# Nothing here is a running total, for the same reason hp and XP are not stored:
# a written-down "18 turns left" is correct for exactly one round and silently
# wrong afterwards. Before this file existed the party had infinite light —
# 1,146 rounds of expedition 4 were run without a single flask being charged.
# THE BURN TIMES ARE NOT IN THIS FILE AND NOT IN THE CODE. They come from
# rules/exploration.md, "Light sources (PHB p. 102, verified)", through
# tools/rules.py — torch 6 turns, lantern 24 turns per pint of oil.
# ORDER IS BY exped/round, NOT BY POSITION IN THE FILE, exactly as
# world_changes.tsv is ordered by exped/turn. The log is append-only, so a row
# backfilled later lands at the bottom; if file order decided the replay, a
# forgotten refill written down afterwards would put the oil in before it was
# burnt. FILL IN `exped` AND `round` — they are the sort key. Ties fall back to
# file order.
# round
#   The ABSOLUTE clock round from campaign/clock.tsv, the same counter
#   tools/clock.py advances. Fuel burns against DUNGEON time, never wall time:
#   10 rounds = 1 turn.
# source
#   A stable id for one physical light source — `lantern-torsat`,
#   `lantern-yrtone`, `torch-3`. Not the carrier: a lantern handed to somebody
#   else is the same lantern and keeps its id and its half-burnt flask.
# kind
#   anchor    sets fuel outright and SUPERSEDES every row above it in game
#             order. Use one when the log cannot be reconstructed further back.
#   new       a source enters play; fuel starts full unless `fuel` says otherwise
#   lit       it is burning
#   hooded    the shutter is closed. IT IS STILL BURNING — rules/exploration.md,
#             "Hooding does not stop the burn". Hooding changes what the dungeon
#             can see, not what the wick consumes.
#   unhooded  the shutter is open again. Also does not change the burn.
#   out       extinguished. THIS is what stops the fuel clock — and it is the row
#             that must be logged before a rest, or the party sleeps through
#             eight hours of lamp oil.
#   refill    a fresh pint goes in. Refusing this on a torch is deliberate: the
#             rules table says "6 turns (1 hour)", naming no fuel, so a torch is
#             a consumed item.
#   spent     fuel written down to nothing by hand (a lamp smashed, oil spilled)
#   lost      dropped, left behind, taken away — it stops being the party's
# what
#   The row it is priced from in rules/exploration.md: "Torch",
#   "Lantern (hooded)", "Bullseye lanthorn", "Magic long sword"…
# fuel
#   TURNS, on anchor/new/refill/spent rows only. Blank on new/refill means "a
#   full one". A literal `?` means UNKNOWN and is reported as unknown — it is
#   never quietly treated as full or as empty.
# certainty
#   `known` (or blank) if the row is a recorded fact. `uncertain` if it is a
#   reconstruction or an assumption; it marks the source uncertain from that
#   point on and every report says so out loud.
when

column1: # Everything above is superseded by the next row, which is where honesty runs
# out. Rounds 173 -> 1146 is 973 rounds, 97 turns. One flask is 24 turns. Had
# Torsat's lantern burned continuously it would have needed FOUR more flasks
# after the one that went in at 173, and only ONE refill was ever mentioned in
# play — Frython, in the trophy room — with THE ROUND NEVER WRITTEN DOWN. So
# either the lamp spent long stretches out (likely: the party has a second
# lantern, eight torches, and has rested) or refills went unlogged. There is no
# way to tell from the record which, and inventing a number here would put a
# confident falsehood into the one file that is supposed to be authoritative.
# The 26 flasks in campaign/inventory.tsv are NOT in doubt; what is in doubt is
# how much of a flask is in each lamp right now.
# FOR THE DM: this resolves the first time somebody looks at a lantern in play.
# Rule the level, log an `anchor` with certainty=known, and this uncertainty is
# gone for good.
